  "title": "GatedRubric-GRPO: Continuous Hierarchical Gating for Non-Verifiable Multimodal Scientific Reasoning",
  "core_problem": "Reinforcement learning with structured rewards has advanced rapidly across three converging axes: (1) gated/hierarchical rewards for verifiable multimodal tasks (PaLMR, PEARL, CogFlow use binary visual gates; VGPO uses a binary Visual Gate for attention compensation), (2) rubric-based RL for non-verifiable tasks (RaR [ICLR 2026] uses rubric rewards with GRPO for medicine/science; DRO uses binary rubric-gates as feasibility constraints; Training AI Co-Scientists applies rubric RL to scientific plan generation), and (3) perception-aware VLM training (VPPO, PAPO, From Seeing to Thinking [ICML 2026] demonstrate perception-first training is critical; Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking [ICML 2026] introduces MoCA for perception-reasoning credit assignment). However, ALL existing gating mechanisms in RL training — whether for visual fidelity (PaLMR), rubric feasibility (DRO), essential criteria qualification (rDPO), or visual attention compensation (VGPO) — employ BINARY gates: hard accept/reject, pass/fail. Separately, works exploring continuous alternatives to binary rewards have shown strong empirical benefits: ReDit demonstrates 10× faster convergence when adding noise to make discrete rewards continuous (with formal optimization time bounds in Theorem 1); Gradient Starvation in Binary-Reward GRPO shows 69% of GRPO groups become degenerate (zero-advantage) with binary rewards at group size 4; and Smooth Operator demonstrates that sigmoid-shaped continuous rewards improve VLM GRPO by +5.6% over binary baselines when combined with absolute-preserving advantage estimation (AP-GRPO). Meanwhile, Grounding the Score uses the sigmoid formula α(r)=σ(β(r−τ)) for inference-time calibration of visual reliability in process reward models — the same functional form we propose for RL training. The problem is especially acute for non-verifiable scientific visual reasoning — tasks like scientific figure explanation, graph-based analytical interpretation, and figure critique — where both visual grounding quality and reasoning quality are INHERENTLY CONTINUOUS and GRADED. A figure can be 70% correctly perceived; a scientific explanation can be partially valid. Binary gating discards this graded signal.",
  "opportunity": "The landscape reveals a specific technical gap at the intersection of four established directions, each now well-validated independently. Direction 1: Gated multimodal rewards exist (PaLMR, PEARL, CogFlow, VGPO) but use binary gates on verifiable tasks. Direction 2: Rubric-based non-verifiable RL is now established — RaR (ICLR 2026) demonstrates up to 31% improvement on medical reasoning with rubric rewards via GRPO, but uses flat weighted aggregation without gating or hierarchical structure. DRO uses binary rubric-gates but is text-only. Direction 3: Perception-aware VLM training is validated — From Seeing to Thinking (ICML 2026) proves that 86.9% of VLM errors stem from perception failures and that perception-first staged training yields +4.6pp improvement; Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking (ICML 2026) shows MoCA credit assignment between perception and reasoning; PAPO finds 67% of failures from perception errors. Direction 4: Continuous rewards/gating mechanisms outperform binary ones empirically — ReDit provides formal bounds showing optimization time scales inversely with reward variance (Theorem 1), Smooth Operator achieves +5.6% with sigmoid continuous rewards for VLM GRPO (though CRITICALLY requires AP-GRPO to prevent signal dilution under group normalization), and Smooth Gate Functions formalizes four axioms for admissible gate functions. The crucial synthesis combines two observations: (A) Scientific visual reasoning exhibits an epistemic dependency — visual grounding is a NECESSARY CONDITION for valid reasoning (you cannot produce a correct explanation of a misperceived figure) — creating a natural gating hierarchy validated by From Seeing to Thinking and Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking. (B) Continuous gating is empirically superior to binary gating, supported by multiple independent results (ReDit, Gradient Starvation, Smooth Operator), because binary gating produces degenerate zero-gradient groups and discards graded quality signals. We present continuous gating superiority as a well-motivated hypothesis — supported by convergent empirical evidence — that our ablation suite (A2/A3 comparing continuous vs binary) will directly validate in the non-verifiable multimodal setting. The sigmoid gating formula g(x)=σ((x−τ)/T) has been applied at inference-time for visual reliability calibration (Grounding the Score) but never integrated into RL training rewards for non-verifiable tasks. Where RaR demonstrates rubric RL for non-verifiable science with flat aggregation, we add hierarchical gating to encode the epistemic dependency. Where Smooth Operator demonstrates continuous sigmoid rewards for verifiable VLM tasks, we extend to non-verifiable scientific reasoning with multi-tier structure. Additionally, POW3R demonstrates that static rubric weights are suboptimal because criteria saturate or become unreachable at different training stages — motivating policy-aware adaptive gating. And Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL reveals systematic exploitation patterns in rubric rewards for scientific/medical domains — motivating our integration of the self-internalization gap as a training diagnostic.",
  "landscape": "PERCEPTION-AWARE RL FOR VLMs: VPPO (arXiv:2510.09285, ICLR 2026) uses Trajectory Advantage Shaping and Token Gradient Filtering based on KL-divergence visual dependency — verifiable tasks only, no explicit gating. VGPO (arXiv:2604.09349, ACL 2026) introduces a binary Visual Gate with attention compensation to counteract temporal visual forgetting — verifiable tasks, binary indicator gate. PAPO (arXiv:2507.06448, ICLR 2026) adds Implicit Perception Loss via masked-image KL divergence and Double Entropy Loss to prevent KL_prcp hacking — verifiable tasks, finds 67% of failures from perception. From Seeing to Thinking (arXiv:2605.20177, ICML 2026) decouples perception and reasoning into staged GRPO training, proving perception-first ordering yields +4.6pp and that 86.9% of errors are perceptual — strongest validation of perception→reasoning dependency but uses hard stage boundaries, verifiable. Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking (arXiv:2605.14054, ICML 2026 Spotlight) introduces MoCA for modality-aware credit assignment via blindfolded reasoning proxy — discrete routing, verifiable. PRCO (arXiv:2603.28618) splits VLM into Observer/Solver roles with differentiated rewards — verifiable, dual-role architecture. Perception-R1 (arXiv:2506.07218) adds visual perception reward to RLVR — verifiable. Vision-SR1 (arXiv:2508.19652) decomposes VLM reasoning with self-rewarding — verifiable. ALL of these address verifiable tasks only; our work extends perception-aware gating to non-verifiable settings. CONTINUOUS REWARD AND GATING MECHANISMS: Smooth Operator (arXiv:2601.07695) proposes SNRA — a dynamically parameterized sigmoid function transforming numerical errors into continuous rewards for VLM GRPO on verifiable spatial tasks. CRITICAL FINDING: smooth sigmoid rewards under vanilla GRPO's group normalization suffer from advantage collapse because relative normalization washes out fine-grained differences; AP-GRPO (Absolute-Preserving) is required to unlock gains (+5.6% over binary). Grounding the Score (arXiv:2603.16253) uses α(r)=σ(β(r−τ)) with β=10, τ=0.5 to gate PRM step rewards by visual reliability — INFERENCE-TIME ONLY calibration for best-of-N reranking, no RL training, structurally identical sigmoid formula to our g_k(x). VL-MDR (arXiv:2604.05445) uses visual-aware gating to dynamically select and weight 21 fine-grained reward dimensions — closest architectural analogue at reward modeling level, DPO-based not RL. ReDit (arXiv:2506.18631) adds zero-mean noise to discrete rewards making them continuous; Theorem 1 proves optimization time lower-bounded by inverse of reward variance; Proposition 1: dithered rewards produce unbiased gradients; achieves GRPO-equivalent performance in 10% of steps; +1.5-4.5 points across 6 models. Gradient Starvation in Binary-Reward GRPO (arXiv:2605.07689) shows binary rewards cause 69% degenerate groups at G=4 (zero advantage); Proposition 2 proves D_real >= p^G + (1-p)^G by Jensen's inequality. Smooth Gate Functions (arXiv:2602.19345) formalizes four axioms for admissible gate functions (continuous differentiability, on-policy maximum, monotonic attenuation, outlier suppression); smooth gates acquire format 4× faster and prevent entropy decay. PEPO (arXiv:2603.22847) uses smooth gating for multimodal token-level advantage estimation. VERIFIABLE MULTIMODAL + GATED/STRUCTURED REWARDS: PaLMR (arXiv:2603.06652) uses gated hierarchical reward R = S_vis·(α·S_ans + (1-α)·S_fmt) where BINARY visual fidelity gates answer reward — closest gating principle but verifiable with binary gate. SR-MCR (arXiv:2512.22545) integrates five sub-rewards with GRPO — flat combination, verifiable. RuCL (arXiv:2602.21628) stratified rubric-based curriculum — verifiable. PEARL (CVPR 2026) binary perception-reasoning gate. CogFlow (ICLR 2026) Visual-Gated Policy Optimization — binary gate. Faithful GRPO (arXiv:2604.08476) spatial grounding — verifiable. Vero (arXiv:2604.04917) task-routed rewards — verifiable. V-Triune (arXiv:2505.18129) sample-level reward routing — verifiable. NON-VERIFIABLE RUBRIC-BASED RL: RaR 'Rubrics as Rewards' (arXiv:2507.17746, ICLR 2026, Scale AI) — PUBLISHED ICLR 2026 paper doing rubric-based RL (GRPO) for non-verifiable science/medicine. Uses instance-specific rubrics with Essential/Important/Optional/Pitfall weighting. Implicit aggregation outperforms explicit per-criterion evaluation. Up to 31% improvement on HealthBench. NO gating mechanism — flat weighted aggregation. Most directly relevant published work; we extend with hierarchical gating + multimodal scientific figure reasoning. DRO (arXiv:2506.13351) BINARY rubric-gating as hard feasibility constraints — text-only. Training AI Co-Scientists (arXiv:2512.23707) rubric RL for scientific plan generation — text-only. Rubric-ARM (arXiv:2602.01511) — text-only. Writing-Zero (arXiv:2506.00103) pairwise GenRM — text-only. Rubric-Grounded RL (arXiv:2605.08061) — text-only. RubricEM (arXiv:2605.10899) — text-only. ARES (arXiv:2605.23454) automated rubric synthesis at scale — text-only. AutoRubric-R1V (arXiv:2510.14738) auto-constructs rubrics for multimodal reasoning with self-aggregation and dual reward integration. NON-VERIFIABLE MULTIMODAL: RubiCap (arXiv:2603.09160) rubric-guided RL for dense captioning — no gating. ClaimDiff-RL (arXiv:2605.20278) claim-level decomposition with graded severity. rDPO (arXiv:2604.13029) rubrics for multimodal DPO — DPO not RL. REWARD DYNAMICS: Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL (arXiv:2605.12474) three exploitation patterns; self-internalization gap (r=0.91-0.97). POW3R (arXiv:2605.20164) policy-aware rubric weighting outperforms static. Reward Design for Physical Reasoning (arXiv:2604.13993) accuracy > flat rubric on verifiable, but rubric improves reasoning quality. GRADIENT THEORY (CORRECTED): Razin et al. (arXiv:2310.20703, ICLR 2024) prove that RL finetuning gradients vanish when reward standard deviation under the model is small, due to the interaction between the reward objective and the softmax operator — motivating reward designs that maximize within-group variance, which continuous gated rewards naturally provide. GR3 (arXiv:2603.10535) addresses length inflation via multiplicative rescaling; notes in Appendix A that multiplicative shaping subsumes heuristic binary gating in binary-reward settings — concerns length control, not hierarchical quality gating. THE GAP: No work combines (1) continuous hierarchical gating in RL training (sigmoid gating exists only at inference-time in Grounding the Score and for verifiable VLM tasks in Smooth Operator; all RL training gating is binary) with (2) non-verifiable rubric-based RL (RaR does rubric RL for non-verifiable science but with flat aggregation, no gating) with (3) multimodal scientific reasoning requiring perception→reasoning dependency (validated by From Seeing to Thinking, Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking, PAPO, but only exploited in verifiable settings) with (4) policy-aware adaptive weight/threshold scheduling with signal preservation.",
  "inspired_by": "Synthesis of convergent empirical evidence across four established directions. RaR (ICLR 2026) demonstrates rubric-based GRPO works for non-verifiable science but uses flat aggregation without gating — we add hierarchical structure encoding the perception→reasoning epistemic dependency. From Seeing to Thinking (ICML 2026) proves perception is a prerequisite scaffold (86.9% of errors are perceptual) but uses hard stage boundaries on verifiable tasks — we implement this dependency as continuous gates within a unified RL objective for non-verifiable tasks. Smooth Operator demonstrates sigmoid continuous rewards improve VLM GRPO on verifiable tasks but requires AP-GRPO to prevent signal dilution — we extend to non-verifiable scientific reasoning and incorporate absolute-preserving advantage estimation. Grounding the Score uses the identical sigmoid formula α(r)=σ(β(r−τ)) for inference-time visual reliability gating — we deploy the same functional form within the RL training loop where it shapes gradient dynamics. Multiple empirical results converge to support continuous > binary: ReDit (Theorem 1: optimization time ∝ 1/reward_variance; 10× convergence speedup), Gradient Starvation (69% degenerate groups with binary rewards), Smooth Gate Functions (4 axioms for admissible gates). We frame this as a well-motivated hypothesis validated by our ablation suite, not a proven theorem. POW3R informs policy-aware adaptation. Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL informs anti-exploitation monitoring. PaLMR provides the gating principle (binary visual gate for verifiable tasks); DRO provides binary rubric-gating for non-verifiable text — we generalize both to continuous gating for non-verifiable multimodal. GRPO's compatibility with multi-reward designs (proven by SR-MCR, DRO, RaR, Vero, V-Triune, POW3R) makes it the natural optimization backbone.",
  "approach": "We propose GatedRubric-GRPO, which introduces CONTINUOUS hierarchical gating for non-verifiable multimodal scientific reasoning within GRPO training on Qwen3-VL-8B. The key technical innovation over existing approaches: (a) vs RaR (ICLR 2026): adds hierarchical gating encoding perception→reasoning dependency to flat rubric aggregation; (b) vs DRO: generalizes from binary to continuous gating and from text to multimodal; (c) vs PaLMR: generalizes from binary to continuous gating and from verifiable to non-verifiable; (d) vs Smooth Operator: extends continuous sigmoid rewards from verifiable to non-verifiable tasks with multi-tier hierarchical structure; (e) vs Grounding the Score: deploys the sigmoid gating formula within RL training (affecting gradient dynamics and policy optimization) rather than inference-time calibration.

CONTINUOUS GATING FORMULATION: The composite reward decomposes into three epistemically dependent tiers:

R = w₁·R₁ + w₂·g₁(R₁)·R₂ + w₃·g₁(R₁)·g₂(R₂)·R₃

where g_k(x) = σ((x - τ_k) / T_k) are sigmoid gate functions with temperature T_k controlling sharpness. This functional form is shared with Grounding the Score's inference-time visual reliability gate α(r)=σ(β(r−τ)) (where T_k = 1/β), but serves a fundamentally different purpose: shaping the RL reward landscape rather than calibrating pre-computed scores for reranking. Key properties: (1) As T_k → 0, g_k → binary indicator 𝟙(x ≥ τ_k), recovering DRO/PaLMR-style hard gating — our formulation subsumes binary gating as a limiting case (a straightforward mathematical observation). (2) For finite T_k, g_k is continuously differentiable, producing non-zero gradients at all reward values — contrasting with binary gating which produces zero gradients in degenerate groups (Gradient Starvation: 69% degeneracy at G=4). (3) T_k can be scheduled during training (warm→cool), implementing an explicit curriculum from exploration to exploitation aligned with From Seeing to Thinking's finding that perception-first ordering matters.

SIGNAL PRESERVATION (addressing Smooth Operator's critical finding): Smooth Operator demonstrates that sigmoid continuous rewards combined with vanilla GRPO's group normalization suffer from advantage collapse — the relative normalization washes out fine-grained continuous differences, requiring AP-GRPO (Absolute-Preserving GRPO) to unlock gains. We address this in two ways: (a) In our setting, base rewards R₁, R₂, R₃ are already continuous LLM-judge scores (unlike Smooth Operator which transforms binary {0,1} rewards into continuous), providing natural within-group variance that is more resistant to normalization dilution. (b) GatedRubric-GRPO+ incorporates AP-GRPO-inspired absolute preservation: the advantage is formulated as a product of relative rank and absolute scalar, ensuring fine-grained hierarchical differences are preserved through GRPO's group normalization. We ablate this component explicitly (A9).

TIER-1 (Visual Grounding, continuous 0-1): Inspired by ClaimDiff-RL's claim-level decomposition and Perception-R1's visual perception reward, we decompose model outputs into atomic visual claims and verify each against the figure. Programmatic checks (element identification, data reading, spatial description) combined with lightweight LLM verification produce a continuous grounding score.

TIER-2 (Structural Quality, continuously gated on Tier-1): A frozen LLM judge (Qwen3-32B) evaluates logical coherence, evidence-claim alignment, domain terminology, and visual-textual consistency using discipline-specific rubric templates following RaR's rubric design principles (self-contained criteria, expert grounding, importance weighting with Essential/Important/Optional/Pitfall categories following Dr.SCI). Rubric templates auto-generated following ARES's pipeline, then expert-calibrated. Continuously gated by g₁(R₁): when visual grounding is poor, structural quality reward is smoothly attenuated (NOT zeroed as in binary gating), providing gradient signal proportional to grounding quality.

TIER-3 (Reasoning Quality, continuously gated on Tier-1 AND Tier-2): Bootstrapped pairwise comparison within GRPO rollout groups assesses analytical depth, interpretive insight, explanation completeness — extending Writing-Zero's BRPO to multimodal. Continuously gated by g₁(R₁)·g₂(R₂).

POLICY-AWARE ADAPTIVE VARIANT (GatedRubric-GRPO+): Inspired by POW3R's finding that static rubric weights are suboptimal, we implement an adaptive variant where: (a) per-criterion contrastiveness is computed from rollout variance within each GRPO group, (b) weights w₁, w₂, w₃ and temperatures T₁, T₂ are rescaled based on criterion contrastiveness with EMA smoothing, (c) category-level normalization preserves the tier structure, and (d) AP-GRPO-inspired absolute preservation prevents signal dilution.

ANTI-HACKING MONITORING: Integrating the self-internalization gap from Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL, we compute the divergence between the policy's prompt-only distribution and rubric-conditioned distribution using only policy log-probabilities. This provides a verifier-free early-stopping diagnostic (r=0.91-0.97 correlation with reference panel).

TRAINING TASKS (genuinely non-verifiable):

(1) Scientific figure explanation generation using MMSci (Nature Communications figures, 72 disciplines) — 10K stratified sample across 18 discipline groups. RE-ANNOTATION PIPELINE: Reference captions decomposed into atomic claims by Qwen3-32B, converted to per-figure rubric criteria across 7 dimensions: Visual Accuracy, Sub-figure Coverage, Quantitative Fidelity, Scientific Terminology, Methodological Context, Interpretive Validity, Structural Description. Each criterion assigned severity following RaR's Essential/Important/Optional/Pitfall categorization. Teacher committee of 3 VLMs generates alternative captions for consensus extraction. MOTIVATION: CIDEr scores are 0.00-3.73 across ALL models on MMSci, demonstrating reference-based metrics are fundamentally inadequate.

(2) Open-ended scientific graph analysis using SciGraphQA re-annotated with rubric scoring.

(3) SciCritique-5K: A new benchmark of ~5K scientific figure critique examples. CONSTRUCTION PIPELINE: (a) Source: ArXiv papers (2020-2025) across 5 STEM domains. (b) Figure type classification using SigLIP visual encoder. (c) Critique generation: 3-model ensemble. (d) Rubric dimensions (8). (e) Each dimension: 5-point ordinal scale + Essential/Important/Optional/Pitfall classification (Dr.SCI approach, also used by RaR). (f) LLM annotation with 3-run median voting. (g) Expert validation: 20% subset (1K items), 3 annotators, target Krippendorff's α ≥ 0.75.

CONTROLLED COMPARISON: CharXiv and SciFIBench as verifiable baselines.

COMPREHENSIVE ABLATION SUITE (9 conditions):
(A1) Flat composite: R = w₁·R₁ + w₂·R₂ + w₃·R₃ (no gating)
(A2) DRO-style binary rubric-gating: hard accept/reject at rollout-group level
(A3) PaLMR-style binary visual gate: R₁ binarized, indicator function gates
(A4) POW3R-style policy-aware weighting WITHOUT gating: adaptive weights but flat combination
(A5) Dynamic weighting à la RuCL: rubric weights adjust during training but without gating
(A6) Tier-1+2 only (no reasoning quality tier)
(A7) Tier-1+3 only (no structural quality tier)
(A8) Grounding-the-Score-style inference-time gating: train with flat rewards, apply sigmoid gating at inference for best-of-N selection — tests whether training-time gating provides value beyond inference-time reranking
(A9) GatedRubric-GRPO without AP-GRPO absolute preservation: tests whether signal dilution (per Smooth Operator's finding) occurs in our non-verifiable setting with already-continuous base rewards

EMPIRICAL MOTIVATION (NOT formal proofs): We motivate continuous over binary gating through convergent empirical evidence: (1) ReDit Theorem 1: optimization time is lower-bounded by the inverse of reward variance — binary rewards minimize variance in homogeneous groups, slowing convergence; continuous gated rewards produce richer variance. (2) Gradient Starvation: 69% of GRPO groups are degenerate at G=4 with binary rewards. (3) Smooth Operator: sigmoid continuous rewards + AP-GRPO yield +5.6% over binary for VLM GRPO on verifiable tasks. (4) Razin et al. (ICLR 2024): RL finetuning gradients vanish when reward standard deviation under the model is small (due to softmax-reward interaction) — continuous gated rewards increase reward diversity. (5) Smooth Gate Functions: formalizes four axioms for well-behaved gate functions that our sigmoid gates satisfy. Our ablation suite (A2/A3 vs full) directly tests this hypothesis in the non-verifiable multimodal setting.",

CONTINUOUS GATING FORMULATION: The composite reward decomposes into three epistemically dependent tiers:

R = w₁·R₁ + w₂·g₁(R₁)·R₂ + w₃·g₁(R₁)·g₂(R₂)·R₃

where g_k(x) = σ((x - τ_k) / T_k) are sigmoid gate functions with temperature T_k controlling sharpness. This functional form is shared with Grounding the Score's inference-time visual reliability gate α(r)=σ(β(r−τ)) (where T_k = 1/β), but serves a fundamentally different purpose: shaping the RL reward landscape rather than calibrating pre-computed scores for reranking. TIER-1 (Visual Grounding, continuous 0-1): Inspired by ClaimDiff-RL's claim-level decomposition and Perception-R1's visual perception reward, we decompose model outputs into atomic visual claims and verify each against the figure. Programmatic checks (element identification, data reading, spatial description) combined with lightweight LLM verification produce a continuous grounding score.

# GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization

## Problem Identified
The paper identifies a critical flaw when applying Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to multi-reward scenarios. The core issue is that "directly applying GRPO to normalize distinct rollout reward combinations causes them to collapse into identical advantage values," which degrades training signal quality and stability.

## The Method: Decoupled Normalization
Rather than normalizing multiple rewards jointly as GRPO does, GDPO introduces a decoupled approach. This technique treats each reward's normalization independently, preserving their individual characteristics and relative relationships rather than homogenizing them into uniform advantage signals.

## Relationship to GRPO
GRPO serves as the baseline approach that GDPO improves upon. While GRPO was not originally designed for multi-reward contexts, recent work attempted applying it directly. GDPO addresses GRPO's limitations by fundamentally changing how normalization operates across multiple preference signals.

## Key Results
The evaluation spanned three domains:
- **Tool calling**
- **Math reasoning**
- **Coding reasoning**

Performance metrics included both correctness measures (accuracy, bug ratios) and constraint adherence metrics (format compliance, length constraints). Across all tested scenarios, GDPO consistently outperformed GRPO, demonstrating improved convergence behavior and training stability while maintaining generalizability across diverse optimization tasks.

# Perceval: Process Reward Model for Vision-Language Models

## Core Mechanism

Perceval functions as a process reward model enabling "token-level error grounding" by extracting image-related claims from responses and comparing them against visual evidence to identify perceptual errors.

## Integration into RL Training

The approach modifies standard GRPO methodology by applying **token-level advantages** rather than sequence-level ones. This enables targeted penalties on hallucinated spans identified by Perceval, creating more granular supervision signals during training with "perception-intensive supervised training data."

## Claim-Level Error Grounding

Rather than evaluating entire responses, Perceval systematically extracts individual visual claims and validates each against the image content, returning "claims that contain perceptual errors" for correction.

## Token-Level Advantage Mechanism

By pinpointing specific hallucinated segments through token-level analysis, the system applies penalties with surgical precision rather than penalizing entire sequences, allowing the model to learn fine-grained distinctions between accurate and inaccurate perceptual outputs.

## Inference-Stage Application

Beyond training, Perceval assists during generation by truncating erroneous response portions, enabling direct regeneration or reflection on previous outputs with iterative repetition for test-time scaling that "demonstrates consistent performance gains over other strategies, such as major voting."

## Results

The research demonstrates "significant improvements on benchmarks from various domains across multiple reasoning VLMs trained with RL."

# Technical Details of GDPO

## 1. Decoupled Normalization Formulation

GDPO performs group-wise normalization separately for each reward before aggregation:

**Individual reward normalization (Eq. 4):**
```
A_k = (r_k - mean{r_k}) / std{r_k}  for each reward k
```

Then sums normalized advantages and applies batch-wise normalization:
```
A_sum = A_1 + ... + A_n
Â_sum = (A_sum - batch_mean) / (batch_std + ε)
```

## 2. Advantage Collapse Mechanism

With standard GRPO, different reward combinations map to identical advantages. For a simple two-binary-reward scenario with two rollouts, the combinations (0,1), (0,2), and (1,2) "all result in identical normalized advantages of (-0.7071, 0.7071)" while GDPO preserves their distinctions.

## 3. Mathematical Foundation

GRPO aggregates first: `r_sum = r_1 + ... + r_n`, then normalizes globally. This compression loses information because "distinct rollout reward combinations" become "collapsed into identical advantage values."

GDPO reverses this—normalizing each reward independently preserves differences across reward dimensions.

## 4. Key Experimental Improvements

Tool-calling (Qwen2.5-1.5B):
- **2.7% accuracy gain** over GRPO
- **4%+ format compliance improvement**

Math reasoning (DeepSeek-R1-1.5B on AIME):
- **6.3% accuracy improvement**
- **80% reduction** in length-exceeding violations

Coding (DeepSeek-R1-7B):
- **2-3% pass rate gains** across benchmarks
- Substantially lower bug ratios

## 5. Distinct Advantage Groups Preserved

Figure 3 shows GDPO maintains "substantially larger number of distinct advantage groups" compared to GRPO as rollouts or rewards increase, providing "more expressive training signals."

# Faithful GRPO: Technical Breakdown

## 1. Lagrangian Constraint Formulation

The core optimization problem treats task accuracy as the primary objective while enforcing consistency and grounding as hard constraints:

**Primary objective:** Maximize task reward (answer accuracy + format adherence)

**Constraints:** Three independent thresholds:
- Consistency reward R_C ≥ τ_C (binary: does reasoning entail the final answer?)
- Semantic grounding R_S ≥ τ_S (continuous: per-sentence visual accuracy)
- Spatial grounding R_G ≥ τ_G (continuous: bounding-box IoU matching)

The Lagrangian formulation combines these with multipliers: "ℒ(θ,λ)=𝔼[R_task(o)]+λ_C(𝔼[R_C(o)]−τ_C)+λ_S(𝔼[R_S(o)]−τ_S)+λ_G(𝔼[R_G(o)]−τ_G)"

## 2. Dual Ascent Mechanism

The approach uses an adaptive learning process that automatically calibrates constraint weights:

"λ_k ← clip(0, λ_max, λ_k + η_λ·(τ_k − c̄_k))"

**How it works:**
- When constraints are violated (c̄_k < τ_k), multipliers increase, raising pressure
- When satisfied (c̄_k ≥ τ_k), multipliers decrease, reducing emphasis
- This creates an emergent curriculum without manual weight tuning

## 3. Constraint Thresholds

Default values used in experiments:
- τ_C = 0.95 (consistency: 95% of correct-answer samples must have logically coherent reasoning)
- τ_S = 0.95 (semantic grounding: 95% mean sentence accuracy)
- τ_G = 0.70 (spatial grounding: 70% IoU-based bounding box matching)
- λ_max = 5.0 (multiplier upper bound for stability)

## 4. Perception as Reasoning Prerequisite

The framework encodes perception constraints by:

**Masking strategy:** Consistency and grounding rewards are only computed for samples where the model produces correct answers (R_acc > 0). This prevents gaming by generating internally coherent but incorrect answers.

**Decoupled normalization:** Each reward signal is independently group-normalized before combination, ensuring none cancels out due to within-group variance cancellation—"each signal operates on a comparable scale and contributes meaningful gradient."

This positions visual grounding and logical consistency as non-negotiable foundations for trustworthy reasoning.

## 5. Key Experimental Results

| Metric | GRPO-T | FGRPO | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Accuracy | 65.17% | 67.16% | +1.99 pp |
| Inconsistency Rate | 26.1% | 1.7% | −24.4 pp |
| Semantic Grounding | 72.7% | 86.0% | +13.3 pp |

Performance across seven spatial benchmarks shows "FGRPO reduces inconsistency to 1.7% on average, compared to 26.1% (GRPO-T)," with largest gains on MindCube (semantic grounding: +22.8 pp) and OmniSpatial (+21.1 pp).

## 6. Comparison to Simple Gating

Table 2 demonstrates why naive approaches fail:

| Method | Accuracy | Inconsistency |
|--------|----------|---------------|
| GRPO + Additive rewards | 64.97% | 4.22% |
| GRPO + Multiplicative gating | 63.47% | 19.61% |
| FGRPO (decoupled) | 67.16% | 1.73% |

Adding constraint rewards additively "sacrifices accuracy (−0.2%)" while multiplicative gating "accuracy drops by 1.7 points while inconsistency remains at 19.6%." FGRPO's decoupled normalization solves the signal cancellation problem that undermines both approaches, achieving simultaneous improvements in both accuracy and faithfulness.

# Technical Details of Perceval: A Perception-Centric Process Reward Model

## 1. Image-Related Claims Extraction
Perceval employs a structured "think-then-answer" paradigm. The model analyzes each claim in a response within `<think>...</think>` tags, evaluating statements for consistency with visual evidence. Claims are extracted by parsing the model's reasoning process to identify perceptual assertions about objects, attributes, and spatial relations.

## 2. Claims Compared Against Visual Evidence
The comparison mechanism operates through hallucination-focused, step-by-step verification. As stated: *"each statement in o is evaluated for consistency with the visual evidence in v"*. When inconsistencies are detected, Perceval returns problematic spans as exact strings from the original response, formatted as a Python list in its `<answer>` section.

## 3. Token-Level Advantage Computation
The key innovation involves modulating sequence-level signals with error masks. Perceval identifies problematic substrings and constructs a binary mask where `m[i,t]=1` for error tokens. The token-level advantage follows: *"A'[i,t] := A[i] - α·m[i,t]·|A[i]|"*, where α controls penalty strength. Correct tokens retain original advantage; hallucination tokens receive reduced (or more negative) signals.

## 4. RL Training Integration with GRPO
Rather than providing scalar rewards, Perceval intervenes during advantage calculation. The paper notes: *"we substitute A'[i,t] into the GRPO objective in Eq. 2 to add the process supervision."* This preserves sequence-level preferences while explicitly suppressing ungrounded content through fine-grained penalties on identified error spans.

## 5. Key Experimental Results
On the 3B model, improvements over GRPO baseline include: ~4% gains on Visual Search tasks, ~3% on Math/Chart reasoning, and ~1% on perception-intensive benchmarks. ## 6. Relationship to GRPO Training
Perceval extends GRPO by replacing coarse sequence-level rewards with fine-grained token-level supervision. Rather than assigning identical advantage scores to all tokens in a response, it identifies and penalizes only hallucinated spans, enabling more precise credit assignment and addressing the sparse-reward limitation inherent in traditional RLVR approaches.
